title: The Smith Chart
description: Plot impedances as reflection coefficients, read VSWR, rotate along lines and switch to admittances.

study.title: From impedance to a point on the chart
study.body: The Smith chart is the complex Γ plane (|Γ| ≤ 1) with a grid of **normalized** impedances $z = Z/Z_0 = r + jx$ drawn on it. Each $z$ has exactly one point $\Gamma = (z-1)/(z+1)$: the centre is a match (z = 1), the left end a short, the right end an open. The grey grid shows $r$ = 0.2, 0.5, 1, 2, 5 (numbers on the real axis) and $x$ = ±0.2 … ±5 (numbers around the rim).

study.title: Circles of constant r, arcs of constant x
study.body: All points with the same $r$ lie on a circle that touches the open end; $r$ = 0 is the rim. All points with the same $x$ lie on an arc that also starts at the open end and meets the rim at $\pm jx$. The **upper half is inductive** (x > 0), the lower half capacitive, the real axis resistive. To plot $z$ = 0.5 + j1, follow the $r$ = 0.5 circle (blue) to where it crosses the $x$ = +1 arc (orange).

study.title: Reading the VSWR
study.body: Along a lossless line |Γ| stays constant, so all impedances seen along it lie on one circle around the centre: the **SWR circle**. Where it crosses the real axis right of the centre, $r$ equals the VSWR (a voltage maximum, $Z = Z_0\cdot VSWR$); left of the centre $r = 1/VSWR$ (a voltage minimum). So the VSWR is read straight off the $r$ scale.

study.title: Explore: moving toward the generator
study.body: A line of length ℓ multiplies Γ by $e^{-j2\beta\ell}$: |Γ| stays and the angle drops by 2βℓ = 720° · ℓ/λ. The point turns **clockwise** on its SWR circle, one full turn per **λ/2**; toward the load it turns counter-clockwise. Printed charts carry a 'wavelengths toward generator' scale around the rim for this, starting at 0 at the short. Drag ℓ and watch $z_{in}$ (red) leave the load $z_L$ = 0.5 + j1 (blue).

study.title: Admittances on the same chart
study.body: $y = 1/z$ turns Γ into −Γ: the admittance point is the impedance point **mirrored through the centre** (the same as a λ/4 line). Two ways to work with it: plot the mirrored point and read the printed circles as $g$ and $b$, or keep the impedance point and use the mirrored grid, whose circles of constant $g$ touch the short end. Here $z$ = 0.5 + j0.5 (blue) lies on the dashed $g$ = 1 circle, and its mirror image reads 1 − j1 = $y$.

study.title: Worked example
study.body:
$Z_0$ = 50 Ω, $Z_L$ = 25 + j50 Ω, line ℓ = 0.2 λ.
- Normalize: $z_L$ = 0.5 + j1
- $\Gamma_L$ = (−0.5 + j1)/(1.5 + j1) = 0.077 + j0.615 = 0.62∠82.9°
- SWR circle: VSWR = 1.62/0.38 = 4.27
- Rotate clockwise by 0.2 × 720° = 144°: $\Gamma_{in}$ = 0.62∠−61.1°
- $z_{in}$ = (1 + Γ)/(1 − Γ) = 0.78 − j1.38, so $Z_{in}$ = 39.2 − j69.1 Ω
- The circle crosses the right real axis (voltage maximum) after 82.9°/720° = 0.115 λ.

study.title: Explore: lossy lines spiral inward
study.body: On a line with loss the reflected wave is attenuated on the way out **and** back: $\Gamma_{in} = \Gamma_L e^{-2\alpha\ell}e^{-j2\beta\ell}$, so the point spirals toward the centre. In dB the return loss at the input is the load's return loss plus **twice** the one-way cable loss. A long lossy cable makes even a broken (open-circuited) antenna look well matched, so measure close to the load. Drag the loss of this one-wavelength line (two turns).

steps.title: One point per impedance
steps.body: Normalize first: $z = Z/Z_0$. Then $\Gamma = (z-1)/(z+1)$ gives the point. The centre is a perfect match, the left end a short, the right end an open, and the rim holds the pure reactances. Upper half inductive, lower half capacitive.

steps.prompt: Where does $z$ = {{r}} + j({{x}}) sit on the Smith chart?

ask.explanation: $\Gamma_i = \frac{2x}{(r+1)^2+x^2}$ = 2 × ({{x}}) / ({{(r+1)^2}} + {{x^2}}) = **{{gi}}**. It has the sign of $x$: inductive loads sit in the upper half.

steps.prompt: Which point is $z$ = {{r}} + j({{x}})?
steps.explanation: Find the $r$ = {{r}} circle (it crosses the real axis at the label {{r}}) and follow it to the $x$ = {{x}} arc (which meets the rim at j({{x}})): that crossing is $z$, at Γ = {{p0x}} + j({{p0y}}). The other points are traps: $z^*$ = {{r}} + j({{-x}}) (mirrored in the real axis), $1/z$ (mirrored through the centre) and the swapped {{xa}} + j({{s*r}}).

steps.prompt: Read the normalized impedance at the red dot.
steps.explanation: The dot sits on the $r$ = {{r}} circle (crossing the real axis at {{r}}) and on the $x$ = {{x}} arc (meeting the rim at j({{x}})). Upper half means $x$ > 0, lower half $x$ < 0, so $z$ = **{{r}} + j({{x}})**. The value {{r/m}} + j({{-x/m}}) is $1/z$, the admittance.

steps.title: The SWR circle
steps.body: A lossless line keeps |Γ|, so every impedance along it lies on a circle around the centre through the load point. Where that circle crosses the real axis on the right, $r$ = VSWR; on the left, $r$ = 1/VSWR. You read the VSWR directly from the $r$ labels.

steps.prompt: The red dot is a load, the dashed circle its SWR circle. Read the VSWR from the chart (two extra grey circles, $r$ = 1.5 and $r$ = 3, are labelled below the axis).
steps.explanation: Follow the circle to where it crosses the real axis right of the centre (orange dot): it lies on the $r$ = **{{S}}** circle, so VSWR = {{S}}. Check: |Γ| = ({{S}} − 1)/({{S}} + 1) = {{G}} is the circle's radius.

steps.prompt: Every point on the outer circle of the Smith chart is a pure reactance (including the short and the open).
steps.explanation: True. The rim is |Γ| = 1: all power is reflected, so the load absorbs nothing and $r$ = 0. Upper half: inductors, lower half: capacitors, left end: short, right end: open.

steps.prompt: Match each place on the Smith chart to what it means.
pairs: Left end of the real axis
Right end of the real axis
steps.explanation: Γ = 0 at the centre (z = 1), Γ = −1 at the short, Γ = +1 at the open. The rim |Γ| = 1 holds lossless loads: $x$ > 0 (inductive) above the axis, $x$ < 0 (capacitive) below.

steps.title: Rotate toward the generator
steps.body: Adding a length ℓ of lossless line between the load and you turns the point **clockwise** on its SWR circle by 2βℓ = 720° · ℓ/λ. Here the load $z_L$ = 2 + j1 (blue) is moved 0.125 λ toward the generator: a quarter turn, to $z_{in}$ = 1 − j1 (red).

steps.prompt: The blue dot is a load $z_L$ = 2 + j1. Which chart shows (red) the impedance seen **0.125 λ toward the generator**?
steps.explanation: 2βℓ = 720° × 0.125 = **90°**, clockwise (toward the generator). $\Gamma_L$ = 0.447∠26.6° becomes 0.447∠−63.4°, which is $z_{in}$ = 1 − j1. Counter-clockwise would be toward the load; a 45° turn forgets that the wave goes there and back (the factor 2); a half turn is what λ/4 would do.

steps.prompt: A load $z_L$ = {{r}} + j({{x}}) sits at the end of a lossless line. Move {{lf}} λ toward the generator.

ask.explanation: $\Gamma_L$ = {{gr}} + j({{gi}}) = {{G}}∠{{deg(th)}}°. Rotate clockwise by 720° × {{lf}} = {{720*lf}}°: angle φ = {{deg(ph)}}°. Then $r_{in} = \frac{1-|\Gamma|^2}{1 - 2|\Gamma|\cos\varphi + |\Gamma|^2}$ = {{1-G^2}} / {{q}} = **{{(1-G^2)/q}}**.

steps.title: Landmarks on the way
steps.body: One full turn is λ/2, so the chart repeats every half wavelength. A quarter wavelength is half a turn: $z$ becomes $1/z$. Crossing the real axis on the right means a voltage maximum ($r$ = VSWR), on the left a voltage minimum ($r$ = 1/VSWR); they are λ/4 apart.

steps.prompt: The load $z_L$ = {{r}} + j({{x}}) is blue. Drag the line length until the input impedance (red) is purely real with $r$ < 1: the first voltage **minimum**.
steps.explanation: $\Gamma_L$ = {{G}}∠{{deg(th)}}°. The voltage minimum is where the SWR circle crosses the real axis on the left (angle ±180°). Turning clockwise from {{deg(th)}}° to −180° takes {{deg(th)+180}}°, so ℓ/λ = {{deg(th)+180}}/720 = **{{lmin}}**. There $r_{in}$ = 1/VSWR = {{(1-G)/(1+G)}}.

steps.prompt: Moving along the line from the generator toward the load turns the point counter-clockwise on the Smith chart.
steps.explanation: True. Toward the generator is clockwise ($\Gamma$ gets the factor $e^{-j2\beta\ell}$); going back toward the load undoes that rotation, so it is counter-clockwise. This is how you find a load from a measured voltage minimum.

steps.prompt: A line ends in $z_L$ = {{r}} + j({{x}}). How far from the load (in wavelengths) is the first voltage **maximum**?
steps.explanation: $\Gamma_L$ = {{gr}} + j({{gi}}), at angle θ = {{deg(th)}}°. The maximum is where the circle crosses the real axis on the right (angle 0°). Turning clockwise from θ to 0° (or to −360°) takes {{mod(deg(th), 360)}}°, so ℓ/λ = {{mod(deg(th),360)}}/720 = **{{lmax}}**. Inductive loads reach the maximum first, within λ/4.

steps.prompt: You measured the VSWR and the distance from the load to the first voltage minimum. Put the steps to find $Z_L$ with a Smith chart in order.
items: Draw the SWR circle through $r$ = VSWR
Mark the voltage minimum: the circle's crossing left of the centre ($r$ = 1/VSWR)
Rotate from there by $\ell_{min}/\lambda$ toward the load (counter-clockwise)
steps.explanation: The VSWR fixes the circle. The measured minimum is a known point on it (left real axis). The load lies $\ell_{min}$ further toward the load, so rotate counter-clockwise by $720° \cdot \ell_{min}/\lambda$, read $z_L$ and denormalize.

steps.prompt: The blue dot is a load $z_L$. If you plot $y_L = 1/z_L$ on the same chart and read its circles as $g$ and $b$, which point do you get?
steps.explanation: $1/z$ changes Γ into −Γ: the admittance point is the load **mirrored through the centre** (the same place a λ/4 line would take it). Mirroring only in the real axis gives $z^*$, mirroring only in the imaginary axis gives $-\Gamma^*$, which is $y^*$. Here $z_L$ = {{r}} + j({{x}}) and $y_L$ = {{r/(r^2+x^2)}} + j({{-x/(r^2+x^2)}}).

steps.prompt: Convert $z$ = {{r}} + j({{x}}) to a normalized admittance $y = g + jb$.

ask.explanation: $y = \frac{r - jx}{r^2 + x^2}$ with $r^2 + x^2$ = {{m}}: $b$ = −({{x}}) / {{m}} = **{{-x/m}}**. An inductive impedance ($x$ > 0) gives a negative susceptance.

steps.prompt: At {{f|Hz}} a load $Z_L$ = {{R}} + j({{X}}) Ω is connected through {{len*1000}} mm of 50 Ω coax with velocity factor 0.66.
The red dot is $z = 1 + jx$; it moves on the $r$ = 1 circle. Drag $x$ until the point lies on the dashed SWR circle for VSWR = {{S}}, on the **inductive** side.
steps.explanation: On the $r$ = 1 circle $|\Gamma|^2 = x^2/(4 + x^2)$. Setting |Γ| = ({{S}} − 1)/({{S}} + 1) = {{G}} gives $x = 2|\Gamma|/\sqrt{1-|\Gamma|^2}$ = **{{xt}}**. This point (1 + j{{xt}}) is exactly where a stub tuner aims: cancel the $x$ and you are matched.

steps.prompt: An antenna has a return loss of {{RLL}} dB at its terminals. You measure it at the far end of a matched cable with {{A}} dB of loss.

ask.prompt: What return loss does the analyzer show?
ask.explanation: The reflected wave crosses the cable twice: RL = {{RLL}} + 2 × {{A}} = **{{RLL+2*A}} dB**. On the Smith chart the point spirals inward.

steps.prompt: Match each change to its effect on the Smith chart.
steps.explanation: 2βℓ = 720° · ℓ/λ: λ/4 is 180° (the λ/4 inverter), λ/2 is 360°. Toward the generator turns clockwise. Loss shrinks |Γ| on the way out and back, so the path spirals inward.

steps.prompt: Start at the open circuit (right end) and move toward the generator along the rim until $z = -j${{x}}. How long (in wavelengths) is this open stub?
steps.explanation: An open stub gives $z = -j\cot\beta\ell$. Setting $\cot\beta\ell$ = {{x}}: βℓ = arctan(1/{{x}}) = {{deg(atan(1/x))}}°, so ℓ/λ = {{deg(atan(1/x))}}/360 = **{{atan(1/x)/(2*pi)}}**. On the chart: the open sits at 0°, the point −j{{x}} at −{{2*deg(atan(1/x))}}°, a clockwise turn of {{2*deg(atan(1/x))}}° = 720° · ℓ/λ.

steps.prompt: On a slotted line the VSWR is {{S}} and the first voltage **maximum** lies {{lm}} λ from the load.

ask.explanation: The maximum is the crossing at $r$ = {{S}} (angle 0°). Rotating back toward the load (counter-clockwise) by 720° × {{lm}} = {{720*lm}}° gives θ = {{720*lm}}° and |Γ| = {{G}}. $r_L = (1-|\Gamma|^2)/(1 - 2|\Gamma|\cos\theta + |\Gamma|^2)$ = {{1-G^2}} / {{q}} = **{{(1-G^2)/q}}**.

ask.prompt: Find the normalized load reactance $x_L$ (with sign).

steps.prompt: A load $z_L$ = {{r}} + j({{x}}) is fed through a matched cable with a one-way loss of {{A}} dB. What VSWR do you measure at the input of the cable?
The blue dot is a load $z_L$ = 0.5 + j1. Which curve is the path of $z_{in}$ as the lossless line grows from 0 to **λ/4**? (The red ring marks the end.)
steps.explanation: λ/4 means 2βℓ = 180°: **half a turn clockwise** on the SWR circle, passing the voltage maximum on the right real axis and ending at $1/z_L$ = 0.4 − j0.8. Counter-clockwise is toward the load; a quarter turn is only λ/8, a full turn λ/2.

steps.prompt: A {{Z0}} Ω line ends in $z_L$ = {{r}} + j({{x}}). You want to cut the line where its input impedance is first purely resistive.

ask.prompt: How long is the line, in wavelengths?
ask.explanation: $\Gamma_L$ = {{G}}∠{{deg(th)}}°. Clockwise, the real axis is reached at 0° (maximum, after {{lmax}} λ) and at ±180° (minimum, after {{lmin}} λ). The first one comes after **{{min(lmax,lmin)}} λ**: a voltage maximum if the load is inductive, a minimum if it is capacitive.

ask.prompt: What resistance (in ohms) do you see there?
ask.explanation: VSWR = (1 + {{G}})/(1 − {{G}}) = {{S}}. The first real point is a maximum ($R = Z_0\cdot VSWR$) for an inductive load and a minimum ($R = Z_0/VSWR$) for a capacitive one. Here $x$ = {{x}}, so $R$ = **{{Z0*if(lmin-lmax, S, 1/S)|Ω}}**.

steps.prompt: On a lossy line, the VSWR measured near the generator is lower than the VSWR right at the load.
steps.explanation: True. The reflected wave loses power on its way back, so |Γ| shrinks toward the generator: the point spirals inward on the Smith chart. The load is no better matched; the cable only hides the mismatch (and wastes the power).

steps.prompt: A shunt element with normalized susceptance $b$ = {{b}} is connected directly across a load $z_L$ = {{r}} + j({{x}}).

ask.explanation: Shunt elements add as admittances. $y_L = 1/z_L$ = {{g}} + j({{bl}}); add j({{b}}): $y'$ = {{g}} + j({{B}}). Back to impedance: $r' = g/(g^2 + b'^2)$ = {{g}} / {{m}} = **{{g/m}}**. On the chart the point slid along the constant-$g$ circle.

ask.prompt: Find the new normalized reactance $x'$ (with sign).

steps.prompt: The red dot is a load on a Smith chart normalized to $Z_0$ = 50 Ω. Which impedance is it?
steps.explanation: The dot is $z$ = {{r}} + j({{x}}) (the $r$ = {{r}} circle meets the $x$ = {{x}} arc). The chart is normalized, so multiply by $Z_0$: $Z$ = **{{50*r}} + j({{50*x}}) Ω**. Forgetting to denormalize, taking the wrong half (sign of $x$) or reading the point as an admittance are the usual slips.
